## Culture and Land-Based Learning

Connect design decisions to place, story, seasons, and respectful observation.

These activities help students notice context before deciding what to make.

### [Grandmother Moon, Seasons, and Turtle's Back](/commons/design-fabrication/culture-land-based-learning/grandmother-moon-seasons.html)

Read seasonal patterns and use a turtle-shell model to organize observations.

Pattern, place, and careful observation support design and environmental learning.

### [Land Lettermark](/commons/design-fabrication/culture-land-based-learning/land-lettermark.html)

Build a lettermark from a place-based observation and document the design choice.

The activity connects visual identity, audience, and responsibility to place.

## N.I.C.E. Design Process

Move from a real situation to evidence, criteria, ideas, feedback, and revision.

The process makes design decisions explainable and repeatable in any project.

### [Understand the Situation](/commons/design-fabrication/design-process/situation.html)

Separate facts, assumptions, and interpretations before defining the problem.

A clear situation prevents a team from solving the wrong problem.

<p class="ter-resource-badges"><a class="ter-resource-badge" href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/19ObkJz3sYVXwB9VkNUiybXZGZ-ihuGw1FarRj81LtAo/copy">Worksheet</a></p>

### [Record User Needs](/commons/design-fabrication/design-process/user-needs.html)

Observe and record what people actually need in the setting.

Evidence about users guides safer and more useful designs.

<p class="ter-resource-badges"><a class="ter-resource-badge" href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/19ObkJz3sYVXwB9VkNUiybXZGZ-ihuGw1FarRj81LtAo/copy">Worksheet</a></p>

### [Necessities and Nice-to-Haves](/commons/design-fabrication/design-process/necessities-nice-to-haves.html)

Separate non-negotiable constraints from preferences.

The distinction keeps safety and function visible when trade-offs appear.

<p class="ter-resource-badges"><a class="ter-resource-badge" href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/19ObkJz3sYVXwB9VkNUiybXZGZ-ihuGw1FarRj81LtAo/copy">Worksheet</a></p>

### [Rank Priorities](/commons/design-fabrication/design-process/rank-priorities.html)

Rank preferences so the most valuable improvements stay visible.

Priorities help a team compare ideas without treating every wish as equal.

<p class="ter-resource-badges"><a class="ter-resource-badge" href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/19ObkJz3sYVXwB9VkNUiybXZGZ-ihuGw1FarRj81LtAo/copy">Worksheet</a></p>

### [Investigate and Inquire](/commons/design-fabrication/design-process/investigate-inquire.html)

Research, observe, measure, collect precedents, and generate several ideas.

Investigation replaces guesses with evidence and expands the possible solutions.

<p class="ter-resource-badges"><a class="ter-resource-badge" href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1c-7TbI3IMOicnHsTUSLkGNJ4s1i2OA6d458S2bTZ2ho/copy">Worksheet</a></p>

### [Create and Communicate](/commons/design-fabrication/design-process/create-communicate.html)

Develop an idea, make the proposal understandable, pitch it, and collect feedback.

Clear communication lets other people test, question, and improve a proposal.

<p class="ter-resource-badges"><a class="ter-resource-badge" href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1T6f3beZhKXiOxS1ecXt3FHbam2yOqeP1yXrmaLFSbAs/copy">Worksheet</a></p>

### [Evaluate and Repeat](/commons/design-fabrication/design-process/evaluate-repeat.html)

Score ideas against necessities and priorities, then revise the strongest option.

Evaluation turns feedback and test results into defensible improvements.

<p class="ter-resource-badges"><a class="ter-resource-badge" href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1O_j4gcsUT0ELFpgJk3GiyG6B1l5brKPko-6lO8HQPfk/copy">Worksheet</a></p>

### [Supply Chain and Life Cycle](/commons/design-fabrication/design-process/supply-chain-life-cycle.html)

Follow a product through materials, manufacture, use, repair, reuse, and disposal.

Life-cycle thinking reveals costs and effects that are easy to miss at fabrication time.

## Logo Design in Photopea

Learn browser-based graphic design by building a nameplate and logo in four short projects.

The sequence develops editable vector artwork for signs, labels, slides, and fabrication.

### [Build the Nameplate Text](/commons/design-fabrication/logo-design/01-nameplate-text-photopea.html)

Make an 11 by 4 inch file, leave room for a logo, and choose readable type.

Correct size, spacing, and legibility prepare a design for real output.

### [Trace a Rough Logo](/commons/design-fabrication/logo-design/rough-sketch-to-svg-photopea.html)

Turn a photographed sketch into clean, editable vector lines.

Tracing converts an idea on paper into artwork that can be revised and fabricated.

### [Combine Logo and Nameplate](/commons/design-fabrication/logo-design/03-combine-logo-nameplate.html)

Combine the ANDRADE logo and nameplate, then export the complete design.

The worked example shows alignment, proportion, and file-export decisions.

### [Design Your Own Name Tag](/commons/design-fabrication/03-laser-cutting/01-name-logo.html)

Apply the tutorial skills to an original name-and-logo design and defend the choices.

The project connects digital design, accessibility checks, and fabrication output.

## Accessible Design

Build accessibility checks into graphic design instead of adding them at the end.

Readable, well-described graphics work better on screens, in print, and on fabricated objects.

### [Access and Alt Text](/commons/design-fabrication/accessible-design/access-and-alt-text.html)

Describe the instructional purpose of an image and identify barriers to access.

Useful descriptions preserve meaning for people who cannot use the image visually.

### [Fonts and Text Effects](/commons/design-fabrication/accessible-design/fonts-and-text-effects.html)

Compare typefaces and test backgrounds, outlines, shadows, and decorative effects.

Legible type survives small screens, printing, engraving, and viewing from a distance.

### [Understanding Colour](/commons/design-fabrication/accessible-design/understanding-colour.html)

Use hue, saturation, value, opacity, and colour models deliberately.

Colour decisions affect emphasis, reproduction, and whether meaning survives greyscale.

### [Contrast and Output](/commons/design-fabrication/accessible-design/contrast-and-output.html)

Check contrast, real size, file type, and final screen, print, or fabrication output.

Testing catches problems before a graphic is shared or made.

## Laser Cutting and Fabrication Tools

Use visual examples, measured drawings, builders, and reusable files to make laser-cut projects.

The tools support measured prototypes, shop organization, and iterative fabrication.

### [Make It Stand](/commons/design-fabrication/03-laser-cutting/02-make-it-stand.html)

Compare ways to support a flat design as a stable object.

Support geometry is useful for signs, displays, holders, and models.

### [Measure and Place](/commons/design-fabrication/03-laser-cutting/03-measure-place.html)

Measure a real object and place openings and supports from evidence.

Measured placement improves access, spacing, and fit.

### [Material Fit and Calibration](/commons/design-fabrication/03-laser-cutting/04-material-fit-calibration.html)

Test material thickness, kerf, and fit before cutting a full project.

Calibration reduces wasted material and unreliable joints.

### [Assemblies and Hybrid Fabrication](/commons/design-fabrication/03-laser-cutting/05-assemblies-hybrid-fabrication.html)

Combine cut parts, fasteners, and other processes into an assembly.

Hybrid fabrication expands what a flat-sheet process can make.

### [Wall and Bench Tool Module](/commons/design-fabrication/03-laser-cutting/07-wall-bench-module.html)

Design a visible, labelled, stable holder for a wall or workbench.

Good tool storage improves access, accountability, and shop safety.

### [Design and Fabrication Capstone](/commons/design-fabrication/03-laser-cutting/08-capstone.html)

Plan, prototype, test, and document an original fabricated solution.

The capstone combines evidence, design decisions, fabrication, and evaluation.
